name: THE FRIENDLY NEIGHBORHOOD
message:
Take a picture and transform it into a warm, gentle scene from the original, beloved children's television program, Mr. Rogers' Neighborhood, in the tradition of the quiet, unhurried neighborhood-host shows of the 1960s-1980s. Place the subject as a warm, invented neighborhood host figure — cardigan sweater being buttoned or already on, sneakers being changed at the door, a soft-spoken, unhurried demeanor — welcoming the viewer into a cozy, handmade television set built from warm wood tones, painted backdrops, and practical household props, NOT a specific existing published or broadcast show's exact set design, characters, or puppets.

ADDITIONAL INSTRUCTIONS
This must read as a lovingly-made ORIGINAL production — invent your own distinct sweater pattern/color, your own trolley-adjacent or vehicle-adjacent transition device if included, and your own puppet/neighbor characters with clearly different names, designs, and personalities from any existing real program. The overall feeling should be warmth, patience, and unconditional kindness — a slower pace than modern children's television, direct warm eye contact with the camera, simple honest language implied through gentle expression.

NEGATIVE PROMPT
fast cuts, frantic pacing, flashy CGI, modern smartphone-era production values, cynicism, sarcasm, loud aggressive colors, corporate slickness, any specific real broadcast show's exact character names, puppet designs, set layout, or branding.

RANDOMIZATION RECOMMENDATION
Yes. Mixing the specific WARMTH_MOMENT beats with the specific SET_DETAIL treatments produces a wide, varied set of cozy scenes while keeping the entire preset anchored to one consistent, original gentle-neighborhood identity.

CREATIVE STRATEGY
This preset uses two internal variable axes merged into one flat options list per the app's schema: options 001-010 are WARMTH_MOMENT (the specific gentle beat being depicted), and options 011-020 are SET_DETAIL (the specific practical, handmade production texture). The fixed, unchanging parameters are the cardigan-and-sneakers ritual, the unhurried pace, and the original-character rule. The variables are the specific moment and the specific set texture layered on top of that fixed identity.

VISUAL DNA ANALYSIS
Cinematic Identity: Warm public-television children's programming — soft 16mm-adjacent broadcast texture, not slick modern video.
Atmosphere: Calm, patient, unconditionally kind, unhurried.
Framing Tendencies: Static or slow-pan camera, direct-address medium shots, warm practical lighting.
Emotional Tone: Safety, gentleness, being truly listened to.
Material Language: Knit wool, varnished wood, painted matte backdrops, felt and yarn puppet textures, soft incandescent light.
Color Relationships: Warm mustard, forest green, and rust tones against soft cream backgrounds, gentle and never garish.
Visual Storytelling: Slowness and ritual — the simple act of changing shoes or buttoning a sweater is itself the story, not a transition to skip past.
